videos.caption: The one prompt edit with Claude, step by step. No DM for resources, it's all right here. 1. Install Claude Code (Codex works too). Download the desktop app. 2. Open Claude Code. It opens in Chat, so switch it over to Code. 3. Make a folder on your computer. Mine is called My Boss Editor. 4. Select the folder: Local, then Open folder. That's your workspace. 5. Copy these GitHub repositories: • FFmpeg: every cut, crop, mix, mute and render · github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg • faster-whisper: word-level transcription every cut is placed against · github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper • Whisper: OpenAI's speech model that faster-whisper runs · github.com/openai/whisper • yt-dlp: downloads the source video · github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp • OpenCV + contrib: follows whoever is talking in the vertical crop · github.com/opencv/opencv and github.com/opencv/opencv_contrib • Puppeteer: headless Chrome that renders the captions and titles to video · github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer • HyperFrames: agent-built motion graphics from HTML · github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes 6. Prompt Claude and give it the links: "You are my short form editor. Here are all the GitHub links to help you do your job." 7. Find an edit you like and send it: "I like the style of this reel. Can we duplicate this style and use it for a video of mine?" 8. Shoot your video. 9. Send it to Claude. Copy the path of the file and paste it in. 10. Review it and use your voice to edit. Bonus: turn it into a skill. "Hey, turn this into a skill." Next time it knows the process. This was not me going into a timeline. Claude edited it in the same list style as the reel I sent it. The 6 levels of AI (and why you can't skip one) Most people think they're good at AI because they use it every day. That's level one. There are six. You don't use it. You tried it once, got something generic, and decided it's overhyped. Chat. Ask, get an answer, copy it somewhere. It saves minutes, but every chat starts from zero. Context. Write one page about your work: who you are, your customers, how you write, what good looks like. Stop rewriting the prompt. Projects and skills. The page lives in a project with your files. Your repeatable jobs become skills, so the AI follows your steps the same way every time. Automations. A new lead gets a drafted reply before you open your laptop. A late invoice gets a reminder on day three. You stop being the trigger. Agents. Give it a goal, not steps. It plans, uses your tools, checks its own work, and asks you before anything important. A team of AI employees. Each one has a lane, its own instructions, tools and memory. They hand work to each other and tell you what needs you. The part that matters: every level sits on the one under it. Context makes skills work. Skills make automations reliable. Reliable automations are what agents use. Find your level honestly, then do the next one. Not the top one. Inside my community I have every level, in order, in eight courses, from your first chat to a team of AI employees. Hit follow and share your most UNHINGED tip! Automation comes last, not first. Asking AI for an answer is stage 1. The work gets more useful when you use AI to test ideas, learn your process, and handle bigger jobs with clear rules. The 5 stages: 1. Ask AI: Get an answer. 2. Think with AI: Find gaps in your ideas. 3. Teach AI: Show it how you like work done. 4. Delegate to AI: Give it a meaningful assignment. 5. Automate with AI: Have it repeat the work on a schedule. At stage 2, ask AI to find blind spots and question whether the work needs to exist. At stage 3, give AI context, examples, rules, and feedback. Let it ask questions. Check the output, then save your process as a reusable skill. At stage 4, give AI a real job with several files. Check every figure and piece of evidence before you trust the result. At stage 5, schedule a reliable skill. Start with drafts for human review. Add tools or connectors when the job needs fresh data. Get the full 5-stage guide here: https://www.sabrina.dev/p/5-stages-of-ai-mastery What are the 5 stages of AI mastery? How do I teach AI how I work?
